readings.title: The drill that stayed in the box
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Willow Library first bought tools after residents said that buying equipment for one small job was expensive. During the first month, drills were borrowed often, but a carpet cleaner remained on its shelf. Staff initially thought nobody needed it. A visitor then explained that its instruction sheet was difficult to follow. The library added a short demonstration on Saturday mornings, and requests increased. This did not prove that demonstrations would help every item. Some tools were simply unsuitable for small flats. Staff began asking borrowers what prevented them from using an item before deciding what to purchase next.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A shelf for unfinished projects
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Nora started a weekly sewing circle for people whose repairs had remained unfinished for months. At first she prepared a different lesson every week. Members, however, brought broken zips and loose hems that did not match her plan. Nora replaced most lectures with a shared work table. Participants could still request a short explanation, but they now learnt while solving their own problems. Attendance became more regular. The change required Nora to admit when a repair was beyond her experience. She kept a list of local specialists instead of promising that the circle could fix everything.

readings.title: The cost of a free service
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community centre advertised free access to its printer on weekday mornings. The organisers expected many job seekers, but only a few came. Interviews revealed that some residents travelled a long way and could not afford repeated bus fares. Others cared for children before lunch. The centre added two evening sessions and allowed visitors to reserve a time by telephone. Use increased without any change to the printing fee. Staff concluded that a service could be free at the point of use and still be costly to reach. They kept the morning sessions for people who preferred them.

readings.title: When a borrowing rule changed
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Members of a housing cooperative could borrow a folding trolley for one day. This seemed fair until several residents explained that their shopping trips took place after late shifts. Returning the trolley before the office closed was difficult. The cooperative introduced a secure return cupboard and kept the one-day limit. Late returns fell, although staff still had to inspect the trolley each morning. The new system did not remove borrowers' responsibility for damage. Instead, it made the existing rule easier to follow. A notice beside the cupboard explained how to report a fault immediately.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

A small library can offer more than books. When neighbours borrow tools that they use only occasionally, they save money and reduce waste. However, a lending service needs clear instructions and regular checks. Sharing works best when everyone understands both the benefits and the responsibilities.
translation.referenceAnswer: 小型图书馆提供的不一定只有书籍。邻居们借用偶尔才用得上的工具，既能省钱，也能减少浪费。不过，借用服务需要清晰的说明和定期检查。只有每个人都了解共享的好处以及应承担的责任，共享才能发挥最好的作用。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Introduce a neighbourhood tool-sharing scheme. Explain one benefit, one possible problem, and a practical rule.
writing.sampleAnswer: I would welcome a tool-sharing scheme in our neighbourhood. Many households need a drill or a trolley only occasionally, so sharing could reduce both expense and the space used for storage. It could also give neighbours a reason to meet and exchange practical advice. However, damaged equipment could lead to arguments or unsafe use. I suggest that a volunteer check every item when it is borrowed and returned, with its condition recorded on a simple card. Borrowers should receive clear instructions and should report faults immediately. A short borrowing period would help more people use popular tools. Starting with a small collection would allow the organisers to learn which items residents actually need before buying more.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
